ArchiveConfiguration.description: The `[package.archive]` table bounds archive acquisition before package analysis.

compressed_size.description: Most compressed archive bytes accepted, 1b to 64gb.

expanded_size.description: Most expanded archive bytes accepted, 1b to 64gb.

expansion_ratio.description: Most expanded bytes per compressed byte, before `expanded_size` bounds the result.

extension_size.description:
Most bytes accepted in one GNU or PAX extended header, 1b to 64mb, checked before
the archive reader allocates its contents. An extended header must also fit `member_size`.

member_size.description: Most bytes accepted in one member, 1b to `expanded_size`, at most 64gb.

members.description: Most archive members accepted, including directories, links, and extended headers.

ByteSize.description: A byte size: an integer magnitude with a required unit suffix `b`, `kb`, `mb`, `gb`, or `tb`; units are binary, so `1kb` is 1024 bytes.

manager.description: Package manager or ecosystem name, as `cargo`, `npm`, or `pypi`.

registry.description: Accepted defining registry endpoint. Absent when the registry is unresolved.

requirement.description: The version requirement this entry declares. Set this or `version`, never both.

version.description: The exact version this entry pins. Set this or `requirement`, never both.

DependenciesCollectionConfiguration.description: The `[dependencies.collection]` table bounds dependency input reads and package collection.

directory_entries.description: Most entries returned by one installed environment directory listing.

lockfile_size.description: Most bytes read from one dependency manifest or lockfile, 1b to 64mb.

manifests.description: Most manifests read by one resolver; ancestor comparisons use at most `manifests` squared work.

nesting_depth.description: Most package names one Bun package key nests.

packages.description: Most packages held in one dependency context, within the global API's 20,000 package ceiling.

pin_size.description: Most bytes read from one toolchain or version pin file, 1b to 64mb.

project_size.description: Most bytes read from one standard library project file, 1b to 64mb.

record_size.description: Most bytes read from one installed distribution's `RECORD`, 1b to 64mb.

toolchain_output.description: Most bytes kept from one version probe stream, 1b to 1mb.

DependenciesConfiguration.description:
The `[dependencies]` table. It states whether the dependency context runs the
standard library version probes, how long one probe may take, and which packages the
operator names beside the ones the workspace's manifests and lockfiles state.

collection.description: File, directory, manifest, package, and version probe collection bounds.

command_timeout.description:
Wall-clock bound one standard library version probe may take before it is
killed, 1s to 1h.

packages.description:
Packages carried beside the ones the workspace's manifests and lockfiles state.
Each entry names exactly one of `version` and `requirement`.

resolution.description:
Whether a standard library version probe runs: `auto` runs `rustc --version` or
`node --version` when no pin names the version, `static` reads the pins and project
files alone and runs no program.

DependencyResolution.description:
Whether the dependency context runs the standard library version probes, or reads
the static inputs alone.

oneOf.description:
A standard library version no pin names is read from `rustc --version` or
`node --version`, and the static reading stands when the probe fails.

No program runs. Every standard library version comes from the pins and project
files alone.

DocumentationConfiguration.description:
The `[documentation]` table: which documentation files the index collects beside the
source. By default every Markdown, MDX, reStructuredText, plain text, and notebook file is
collected, except change logs, licenses, codes of conduct, and archived, deprecated, or
translated copies.

enabled.description:
Whether documentation files are collected at all. `false` collects none; the
documentation comments attached to declarations stay.

exclude.description:
Exact file paths or globs whose documentation is left out beside the default
exclusions, in [`PathPattern`] syntax.

force_include.description:
Exact file paths or globs collected although a default exclusion leaves them out, in
[`PathPattern`] syntax. A match `exclude` also names is still left out.

max_file.description: Source bytes one documentation parser accepts.

max_heading_depth.description: Heading levels one documentation block retains.

max_layer_blocks.description: Blocks one documentation layer holds across its collections.

max_mappings.description: Ranking identity mappings one documentation layer holds.

max_nodes.description: Syntax nodes one documentation parser accepts.

max_progress.description: Progress callbacks one reStructuredText parser accepts.

max_references.description: Links, fragments, or reference candidates one collection retains.

max_sources.description: Selected documentation sources one collection accepts.

max_text.description: Bytes one heading, language, destination, or reference spelling retains.

max_total.description: Source bytes one documentation collection accepts together.

Duration.description: A duration: an integer magnitude with a required unit suffix `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, or `d`.

EmbeddedEngine.description: One engine this build links in, served in process without a command.

oneOf.description: The ty type checker, serving Python semantics in process.

EmbeddingConfiguration.description:
The `[search.vector.embedding]` table: which embedding model runs, and
the bounds its execution keeps. `kind` selects the arm, and each arm
carries only the keys its execution reads.

A `directory` model downloads nothing, so it carries no download keys. An
`openai_compatible` model sends declaration text while vectors are built
and query text while a search runs; `api_key_env` names the environment
variable holding the credential and never carries the credential itself.

oneOf.description:
Weights come from a Hugging Face repository, cached where every other
Hugging Face client on the machine caches them.

batch_inputs.description:
Inputs one embedding pass hands the encoder at once, 1 to 256.
Attention memory grows with the square of `max_tokens`, so a
raised token window wants a lowered batch.

download_attempts.description:
Attempts one model download makes before vector ranking degrades
to lexical for the life of the server, 1 to 10.

download_timeout.description: Wall-clock budget one model download has, 10s to 1h.

max_tokens.description:
Tokens the encoder reads from one input, 32 to 512. What follows
them is truncated.

model.description:
A repository identifier such as `minishlab/potion-retrieval-32M`,
optionally carrying a revision after `@`. Vectors are stored per
model, so changing the value embeds the workspace again.

The model's own `config.json` decides how it is read. A
`model_type` of `model2vec` is a static model, which embeds a
declaration by averaging one row per token; anything else is read
as a BERT checkpoint, which runs a forward pass per batch and
costs minutes rather than seconds over a whole workspace.

oneOf.description:
Weights are a directory the workspace already holds. Nothing is
downloaded.

batch_inputs.description: Inputs one embedding pass hands the encoder at once, 1 to 256.

max_tokens.description:
Tokens the encoder reads from one input, 32 to 512. What follows
them is truncated.

model.description: A workspace-relative directory holding the model files.

oneOf.description:
Vectors come from a service implementing the `OpenAI` embedding
request and response shape at `/embeddings`.

api_key_env.description:
The environment variable holding the credential. The value names
the variable; it never carries the credential.

attempts.description:
Attempts one embedding request makes, 1 to 10. Retries spend the
same request timeout.

batch_inputs.description: Inputs one embedding request carries, 1 to 2048.

endpoint.description:
The base URL the request path is appended to. It uses `https`;
`http` is accepted only when the host is a loopback address.

max_in_flight.description: Embedding requests running at once, 1 to 32.

model.description: The model the service exposes, such as `text-embedding-3-small`.

request_timeout.description: Wall-clock budget one embedding request has, 1s to 5m.

revision.description:
A deployment identifier the operator states, such as a dated
release. It participates in vector invalidation, so an endpoint
serving new weights under one model name gets a new value here.

ExecutionConfiguration.description:
The `[execution]` table. Exact language entries enable execution; this
table owns the workspace-wide bounds.

max_code.description: Bytes one submitted block may hold, 1b to 32kb.

max_concurrent.description: Evaluations running at once across the whole workspace.

max_output.description: Bytes each captured stream keeps, up to 16kb.

GlobalConfiguration.description: The `[global]` table: global REST API access, request bounds, and cache lifetimes.

attempts.description: Attempts one global API request makes, 1 to 5.

enabled.description: Whether package reads use the global REST API.

endpoint.description: Base URL for global REST API requests. The client validates its URL form.

max_in_flight.description: Global API requests running at once, 1 to 32.

max_request.description: Most bytes in one global API request body. A larger body is refused before sending.

max_response.description: Most bytes in one global API response body. A larger body is refused while reading.

max_source.description:
Most UTF-8 bytes in one source payload from the global API. The client also applies the
advertised source bound, using the smaller value.

request_timeout.description: Total request timeout across connection, response, delays, and attempts, 1s to 5m.

token_env.description: Environment variable containing the optional bearer token. The client validates its name.

allOf.description: providers.history.strategy selective names at least one release
providers.history.releases belongs to strategy selective alone

HistoryConfiguration.description:
The `[providers.history]` table. The history provider analyzes the revisions its
strategy selects into the history store, one repository-wide store every worktree
reads, and fills it in the background: `max_revisions` bounds what the store holds,
and the batch and CPU-share keys bound what one fill costs the machine. The server
reads the table at startup, so a change applies on the next start.

batch_commits.description: Commits one history store batch writes, 1 to 10000.

batch_size.description:
Parsed bytes one history store batch holds past its first commit, 1kb to 1gb. A
commit that parses more is a batch of its own.

cpu_share.description:
The share of one core the history task parses at, above 0.0 up to 1.0: after each
commit it pauses long enough to hold the share.

enabled.description: Whether the history provider runs at all.

max_revisions.description:
Revisions the history store holds, newest first, 1 to 100000: the first-parent
commits from each worktree's `HEAD` under `everything`, the releases under
`selective`.

move_deletions.description:
Deleted files one history commit pairs for declaration moves, after pure renames,
1 to 65536. A commit past this bound keeps introduced declarations without pairing
moves. Raising the bound increases the work to find each moved declaration.

release_tags.description:
Tags one release selection reads, 1 to 5000000, including tags that name no commit
or match no release pattern. A larger tag set is refused.

releases.description:
Tag names or tag patterns naming the releases `selective` analyzes, such as `v1.*`,
at most 64. The releases order by the version each tag name spells once the
pattern's literal text up to its first digit or wildcard is removed; a tag whose
rest is no version is left out. Only `selective` reads them.

strategy.description: Which revisions the history store analyzes.

tree_entries.description:
Tree entries one revision read visits and changed paths one history commit collects,
1 to 5000000. A larger revision tree is refused; a larger changed-path set makes the
history commit a boundary whose changes are unknown.

HistoryStrategy.description: Which revisions the history store analyzes.

oneOf.description:
The newest `max_revisions` first-parent commits from each live worktree's `HEAD`,
each compared with its first parent.

The newest `max_revisions` of the releases `releases` names, in version order, each
compared with the release before it.

enabled.description: Whether syntax, LSP service, and execution are enabled for matched paths.

exclude.description: Path patterns removed from this language's effective matches.

execution.description: Whether caller-provided code may execute under this exact language.

include.description: Replacement path patterns. Absence keeps shipped patterns; an empty list matches none.

lsp.description: Inline LSP process or name of one shared process.

stdlib.description:
Whether the package context names this language's standard library: `stdlib/rust`
for `rust`, `stdlib/node` and npm `typescript` for `javascript`, `typescript`, and
`typescript:tsx`, and `stdlib/python` for `python`. A library stays in the context
while any language the workspace uses that names it keeps this key on.

anyOf.description: Name of one shared top-level `[lsp.<name>]` process.
Process used only by this exact language entry.

LanguageLspConfiguration.description: How one exact language selects an LSP process.

LargeFileStrategy.description: What the text index does with a file whose text runs past `[search.text] max_chunk`.

oneOf.description:
The file's text is indexed as whole-line chunks of at most `max_chunk` bytes, and a
file past `[providers.syntax] max_file` is held as text the syntax provider does
not parse, up to `[source] workspace_size`.

The file leaves the text index: no search reads its text, and a file past
`[providers.syntax] max_file` leaves the index entirely.

LexicalSearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search.lexical]` table: how many units the lexical index holds, how many one
transaction writes, and how much of the store file a connection memory-maps.

max_content.description:
Most bytes one lexical document content field holds, 1kb to 1gb.
A document past this bound refuses the lexical write.

max_documentation.description:
Most encoded documentation metadata one commit stores, 1kb to 4gb.
A larger collection commits lexical documents without the metadata.

max_matches.description:
Most matches one lexical ranking collects, 1 to 1000000.
An answer past this bound carries `lexical_ranking_truncated`.

mmap_size.description:
How much of the index database each connection reads through a
memory map, 0b to 2147418112b; `0b` reads through `SQLite`'s page
cache alone. Every connection maps the file on its own, so resident
memory counts the mapped pages once per open connection.

transaction_size.description:
Most content one lexical transaction writes, 1mb to 1gb, counted and
applied the way `transaction_units` is.

transaction_units.description:
Most units one lexical transaction writes, 100 to 1000000. A write
larger than this commits in several transactions, and the tree it
answers for is stamped by the last. One file's units always share a
transaction, so a file holding more units takes one of its own. The
trigram index `pattern` search reads is filled after each write in
transactions of at most this many rows.

units_max.description:
Most units the lexical index holds: one per indexed file, text chunk,
and declaration, 1000 to 50000000. A workspace past it refuses its
rebuild naming this key.

LogsConfiguration.description:
The `[logs]` table bounds log delivery, retention, capture, and metric attribute sets.

The server records diagnostics in `.rift/metrics`, where `rift server logs` reads them.
The table also bounds stall reports and standard error that is not a terminal.
The server reads the table at startup, so a change applies on the next start.

capture.description:
Which targets are recorded, in the `RUST_LOG` spelling `tracing` takes:
comma-separated `target=level` pairs. A target this filter excludes
never reaches the store, whatever the stderr diagnostics carry.

cardinality_limit.description: Attribute sets one metric instrument holds before overflow, 1 to 65536.

flush_interval.description: Wait before the drain writes a partial batch, 1ms to 1h.

queue_records.description: Records one log subscription holds before it drops and counts, 1 to 65536.

retention_records.description: Records the store keeps before the oldest are dropped, 100 to 1000000.

retry_interval.description: Wait before the drain retries a batch the store refused, 1ms to 1h.

stall_delay.description:
Age past which an operation, lock wait, or held lock still open is reported
once, as a record of the operations in flight, 1s to 1h.

stderr_limit.description:
Bytes the server's standard error passes, when it is not a terminal, before it
prints one notice and discards the rest, 1kb to 1gb. The log drain's stop records
the bytes discarded.

LspConfiguration.description: One external LSP process Rift may start.

command.description:
Executable and literal arguments. Rift starts it directly without a
shell. Exactly one of `command` and `embedded` is present.

embedded.description:
Engine linked into the server, run in process in place of a spawned
command. Exactly one of `command` and `embedded` is present, and an
embedded engine takes no `environment` and no
`initialization_options`.

environment.description:
Environment values added on top of the environment the server
inherited.

initialization_options.description:
Options handed to the process at initialize. Must be a JSON object
when present; the LSP server defines its meaning.

output_limit.description:
Bytes of the process's standard error Rift keeps, 1kb to 8mb. The
full size is still reported.

request_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound on each later LSP request, 1s to 10m.

restart.description:
How often Rift replaces this process on its own, and over what
window; the budget spent, the process's own failure surfaces.

retry.description:
How often Rift sends this process the same request again while its
answer stays unsettled - a refusal the process invites again, or an
answer it gave while still analyzing - and how the waits between
those attempts grow.

settle_delay.description:
Quiet the process's work record holds before a read calls it ready,
10ms to 1m. A language server empties its outstanding work several
times inside one project load, so Rift reports the process ready only
once that record has been empty this long at the last engine output
Rift read. Raise it for a process whose load falls silent for longer
than the default between phases.

startup_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound on the process's initialize handshake, 1s to 10m.

PackageConfiguration.description:
The `[package]` table: publication capacity for exact-package collection.
Input files, bytes and declarations use `[source]`; parsing uses `[providers.syntax]`.

archive.description: Compressed archive admission before source selection and package analysis.

identifier_terms.description: Most identifier terms retained per search document, 1 to 65536.

retained_source.description: Most source bytes retained per record, 1b to 64mb; larger source is cut.

retained_total.description:
Most retained source bytes across units, symbols and documents, including copies.
Absent preserves the existing aggregate behavior; a selected total must cover one
complete record bound, and collection refuses before allocation passes it.

PathPattern.description:
Project-relative glob using *, ?, **, and character classes. Forward-slash separated on
every platform, whatever separator the host OS uses natively.

PortRange.description:
The `server.port_range` table: the inclusive loopback range the server
picks the first free port from.

max.description: The highest port the server may bind, at or above `min`.

min.description: The lowest port the server may bind, 1024 or above.

ProvidersConfiguration.description:
The `[providers]` table: the built-in providers run without
configuration, and this table bounds or disables them.

syntax.description: The bounds every syntax provider parses one source under.

RankingConfiguration.description:
The `[search.ranking]` table: what each ranking input contributes to a
fused score, and how sharply a top rank counts.

The three weights need not sum to 1. The executor normalizes the weights
of the inputs that answered, so an unavailable vector ranking does not
rescale what identifier matching and the lexical ranking returned.

fusion_k.description:
The reciprocal-rank fusion constant, 1 to 1000. A result scores as the
weighted sum of `1 / (k + rank)` over the rankings that returned it, so
a larger value flattens the contribution curve and lets agreement
between the rankings outweigh one ranking's top position.

identifier_weight.description:
The identifier ranking's share of a fused score, 0.0 to 1.0.
Identifier matching ranks a query against indexed declaration and
qualified names.

lexical_weight.description:
The lexical ranking's share of a fused score, 0.0 to 1.0. The lexical
ranking is the `SQLite` full-text index over declaration names,
signatures, and attached documentation, and over the text of every
indexed file, stored once.

vector_weight.description:
The vector ranking's share of a fused score, 0.0 to 1.0. The vector
ranking answers a query that shares no word with the code it should
reach.

RestartPolicy.description:
How often Rift may replace one language engine on its own, and over
what window.

A restart is any start after the first: the first is the start, and
every start that follows it replaces an engine that ended, failed to
start, or stopped answering. A restart older than `window` no longer
counts, so a workspace whose engine dies once a day keeps its full
budget while a crash-looping one spends it and stops.

attempts.description: Restarts allowed inside one window, 0 to 16. Zero never restarts.

window.description: Span the restarts are counted over, 1s to 1d.

RetryPolicy.description:
How often one unsettled operation is attempted again, and how the
waits between attempts grow.

Attempts are numbered from one and the first is counted, so
`attempts = 1` never resends. Each wait is twice the one before it,
held at `delay_limit`; a `delay_limit` below `delay` therefore holds
every wait at `delay_limit`.

The waits carry no jitter. Jitter spreads a set of independent retriers
apart so they stop arriving together; requests to one language engine
serialize on that engine's own slot, so there is never such a set, and
the sequence stays a function of the attempt number alone.

attempts.description: Attempts one operation takes, the first counted, 1 to 64.

delay.description:
Wait before the second attempt, 1ms to 1m. Every later wait
doubles the one before it.

delay_limit.description: Longest wait between two attempts, 1ms to 10m.

SearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search]` table. `ranking` weighs the ranking inputs against each
other, `lexical` and `vector` bound the two indexed rankings, `text`
bounds the lexical chunks derived from visible text files,
`pool_slots`, `busy_timeout`, and `journal_size_limit` bound the `SQLite`
connections of the index database and of the vectors database, and the
`pattern_` keys bound one regex `pattern` search.

busy_timeout.description:
Wall-clock budget one caller waits for a free pooled connection, and
one connection waits for a database lock held by another process
before `SQLITE_BUSY`, 100ms to 30s.

journal_size_limit.description:
Size the write-ahead log of `.rift/index`, and separately of
`.rift/vectors`, is cut back to at the commit that restarts it after a
checkpoint, 0b to 64gb. A transaction larger than this still grows the
log past it until that commit.

lexical.description: How many units the lexical index holds.

pattern_candidate_rows.description:
Most rows of the trigram index one `pattern` search reads to select the
files it verifies, 100 to 1000000, counted once per chunk of a large file.
A search whose selection passes it is refused naming this key. Rows the
trigram index does not hold yet are verified within what the selection
leaves of it; past that, the search answers from the rows the index holds
and warns `pattern_index_preparing`.

pattern_compiled_size.description:
Most bytes the matcher one search `pattern` compiles to may take, 64kb to
64mb. A pattern whose matcher compiles past it is refused naming this key.

pattern_matches_per_file.description:
Most matches one file contributes to a `pattern` search, 1 to 100000. A
file past it is cut there, and the answer warns
`pattern_matches_truncated`.

pattern_verified_size.description:
Most file text one `pattern` search verifies, 1mb to 64gb. A search that
would verify more is refused naming this key. Rows the trigram index does
not hold yet are left out rather than verified past it, and the answer
warns `pattern_index_preparing`.

pool_slots.description:
Pooled `SQLite` connections the index database may open at once, and
separately the vectors database, 1 to 16.

ranking.description: What each ranking input contributes to a fused score.

results.description:
Most results one local search or symbol lookup collects, 1 to 10000.
An answer that reaches this bound warns `results_truncated`.

symbol_alternatives_lowercase_work.description:
Work units reserved per input byte before lowercase allocation, 12 to 1024.
Twelve covers three lowercase characters of at most four UTF-8 bytes each.
Larger values reserve more work without changing lowercase mappings.

symbol_alternatives_work.description:
Work units one complete closest-declaration ranking may reserve, 1 to 1073741824.
Exhaustion discards all alternatives and reports the configured bound.

text.description: Chunking policy for visible text files in lexical search.

vector.description:
The embedding model that adds vector ranking, and the bounds its
preparation runs under.

allOf.description: server.port and server.port_range are mutually exclusive

ServerConfiguration.description:
The `[server]` table. Filesystem scans and parses run on a bounded
worker pool; this table sets the worker count, bounds the queue wait,
sets how long the server serves with no request before it stops, and
selects the loopback port. The server reads the table at startup, so a
change applies on the next start.

idle_timeout.description:
Wall-clock span after the last served request completes that stops
the server while no request remains active, 1s to 1d.

num_workers.description: Workers running blocking filesystem and parser operations at once, 1 to 64.

port.description:
The exact loopback port the server binds, 1024 or above. Excludes
`port_range`; omitted, the server picks from `port_range` or the
default serving range.

port_range.description:
The loopback range the server picks its port from. Excludes `port`;
omitted, the default serving range applies.

readiness_timeout.description:
Wall-clock bound one request waits for the workspace's index and
its language services to prove they are ready to answer, 1s to 1h.
One deadline: index validation starts it, and once a request
resolves the languages it needs, waiting on those services spends
what remains of it.

validation_interval.description:
Maximum span between background filesystem validations, 1s to 1h.
Requests and filesystem events do not reset this interval.

version_control_timeout.description:
Maximum span publication waits for the worktree's Git index lock,
1ms to 30s. A lock retained past this bound is logged and passed.

worker_queue_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound one request waits for a free worker, 1ms to 1h.

workspaces.description: Workspaces one repository process may retain, 1 to 64.

SourceConfiguration.description:
The `[source]` table: which files below the workspace root the index and reads consider
visible, and how many files, bytes, and declarations the index holds together. `.git`,
`.rift`, and `target` stay invisible whatever this table says.

declarations.description:
Most declarations the index holds together, 10000 to 50000000. A workspace
declaring more publishes the files that fit and leaves the rest out, each one
reported as an unavailable source naming this key.

directory_depth.description:
Most directory levels scanned below the workspace root, 1 to 4096.
A deeper directory refuses the rebuild naming this key.

exclude.description:
Exact file paths or globs dropped from visibility, in [`PathPattern`] syntax. A match
here is dropped even when `include` also matches it.

files.description:
Most files the index holds, 1000 to 5000000. A workspace past it refuses its rebuild
naming this key.

force_include.description:
Exact file paths or globs that stay visible although the workspace's `.gitignore`
hides them, in [`PathPattern`] syntax. A match here needs no `include` match, and a
match `exclude` also names is still dropped.

include.description:
Exact file paths or globs a file must match to stay visible, in [`PathPattern`] syntax.
Empty includes every file `exclude` and `.gitignore` leave standing.

relationships.description: Most relationship edges held together, 1 to 500000000.

respect_gitignore.description:
Whether the workspace's own `.gitignore` files, root and nested, hide the paths they
match. Global and parent-directory gitignore sources are never read.

workspace_size.description:
Most source bytes the index holds together, 16mb to 64gb. A workspace past it
refuses its rebuild naming this key.

SyntaxConfiguration.description:
The `[providers.syntax]` table. A syntax provider's cost scales with the
source it parses, so each source is bounded by size, node count, and
nesting depth; a source past any bound is left out of the index.

frameworks.description:
Explicit framework context for matching source paths. Automatic context reads
the source's own package and component for frameworks a selection does not supply.

max_depth.description: Nesting one source's syntax tree may reach.

max_file.description: Bytes of one source a provider parses, 1b to 64mb.

max_nodes.description: Syntax nodes one source may produce.

SyntaxFrameworkConfiguration.description: One explicit framework context, selected by workspace-relative path patterns.

angular.description: Treat matching HTML sources and owned TypeScript templates as Angular.

include.description: Source paths this context applies to. An empty list selects no source.

tailwind.description: Tailwind major version whose directives and static classes are interpreted.

TailwindVersion.description: Tailwind versions with distinct stylesheet and configuration syntax.

oneOf.description: Tailwind 3 uses configuration files and `@tailwind` directives.
Tailwind 4 uses stylesheet imports, theme declarations, and custom utilities.

TextSearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search.text]` table. `include` selects which visible paths join the
text index once every language entry has had its claim, `max_chunk`
bounds the lexical units derived from them, `large_files` decides what
happens to a file past `max_chunk`, and `excluded_lockfiles` names the
lockfiles the index leaves out of search.

excluded_lockfiles.description:
File names of the lockfiles the index leaves out of search, matched against
each visible file's final path segment. Such a file answers no search and no
symbol lookup, while `rift://map` still reads its pinned versions and
`paths.force_include` still reaches it for one request. An empty list
indexes every lockfile.

include.description:
Project-relative path patterns included as plain text when no language claims them.
The default `["**"]` selects every unclaimed visible path; an empty list selects none.

large_files.description:
What the text index does with a file past `max_chunk`: `split` indexes it in
chunks and holds a file past `[providers.syntax] max_file` as unparsed text;
`skip` leaves it out of the text index, and every search answer whose `paths`
reach one counts it in a `large_file_skipped` warning. Omitted, `split`.

max_chunk.description:
Bytes one lexical chunk may hold, 1kb to 16mb. A larger file is indexed as
several chunks of at most this size, or left out of the text index, as
`large_files` decides.

VectorSearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search.vector]` table: the vector ranking that reaches code sharing
no word with a query, and the bounds its preparation runs under.

Preparation runs behind the answers. A search issued before the vectors
are in is answered lexically and carries a warning naming what is still
missing.

candidates.description:
Declarations the vector ranking returns before the rankings are
fused, 1 to 1000.

candidates_per_file.description:
Declarations one file may contribute to the vector ranking before
the rest of its declarations are dropped, 1 to 64. Without the bound
one file whose declarations all rank well fills `candidates` on its
own, and no other file reaches the candidate list however well it
would have ranked.

disabled.description:
Whether vector ranking is off. Set it when the workspace must not
fetch model weights: search then answers lexically alone and raises no
preparation warning.

embedding.description:
Which embedding model builds the vectors, and the bounds its
execution keeps.

max_vectors.description:
Vectors the workspace may hold, 1000 to 1000000. Embedding stops at the
bound and the search warning says so; each vector costs the model's
dimension in single-precision floats.

description:
The whole `rift.toml`. Every table is optional and defaults to the
behavior documented on it; any key outside these definitions refuses the
file as `configuration_invalid`.

dependencies.description:
Whether the dependency context runs the standard library version probes, how long
one probe may take, and which packages the context carries beside the ones the
workspace's manifests and lockfiles state.

documentation.description: Which documentation files the index collects beside the source.

execution.description: Enablement and limits for caller-provided code.

global.description: Whether package reads use the configured global REST API and its request bounds.

languages.description: Exact language entries keyed by their `name` or `name:dialect` identity segment.

logs.description:
The server's own log records: how many the metrics database keeps,
how many one read returns, and which targets are captured.

lsp.description: Shared LSP processes keyed by name. Language entries select them explicitly.

package.description: Exact-package publication and archive admission bounds.

providers.description: Bounds and switches for the built-in providers.

search.description: Search ranking, visible text chunking, and storage bounds.

server.description: The server's own blocking-work bounds: worker count and queue wait.

source.description:
Which files below the workspace root the index and reads consider visible, and how
many files and bytes the index holds together.
